links.card_of: Rufus: A son of Simon of Cyrene, the man compelled to carry Jesus' cross.

sentences: Matthew lists him among the twelve apostles as Simon the Cananaean (Matthew 10).
Luke calls him Simon the Zealot in his list of the apostles (Luke 6).
links.card_of: Simon the Zealot: One of the twelve apostles, called the Zealot or the Cananaean to distinguish him from Simon Peter.

sentences: The people of Nazareth named Simon among Jesus' brothers, with James, Joseph, and Judas (Matthew 13).
links.card_of: Simon: One of the brothers of Jesus, named by the people of Nazareth when they took offense at him.

sentences: A man of Bethany, known as Simon the leper, at whose home Jesus was anointed shortly before his death.
Shortly before the Passover, Jesus was at the home of Simon the leper in Bethany (Matthew 26).
links.card_of: Simon the leper: A man of Bethany, known as Simon the leper, at whose home Jesus was anointed shortly before his death.

sentences: As Jesus was led out to be crucified, soldiers compelled Simon of Cyrene to carry his cross (Matthew 27).
links.card_of: Simon of Cyrene: A man from Cyrene whom Roman soldiers compelled to carry Jesus' cross to the crucifixion.

sentences: Simon practiced magic in Samaria and amazed the people, who called him the great power of God (Acts 8).
Peter sharply rebuked him and called him to repent, and Simon asked the apostles to pray for him (Acts 8).
links.card_of: Simon: A magician in Samaria who believed Philip's preaching but tried to buy the power to give the Holy Spirit.

sentences: Peter stayed many days in Joppa at the house of Simon the tanner (Acts 9).
An angel told Cornelius to send for Peter, who was lodging with Simon by the sea (Acts 10).
Cornelius's messengers arrived at Simon's gate and brought Peter back with them to Caesarea (Acts 10).
links.card_of: Simon: A tanner in Joppa whose house by the sea hosted the apostle Peter.

options.name: Tubal
options.who: A distant nation descended from Japheth, often paired with Meshech, known for trading slaves and bronze.

options.name: Tubal
options.who: A son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, whose descendants became a distant northern people.

sentences: Assyria, Elam, Meshech, Tubal, Edom, and Sidon already lie in the pit.
Ezekiel prophesied against Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (Ezekiel 38).
links.card_of: Gog: Ruler from the land of Magog whom Ezekiel foresaw attacking Israel in the latter days.

sentences: Tubal is named among distant nations who will hear of the Lord's glory (Isaiah 66).
Tubal traded slaves and bronze vessels with the city of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Gog is called chief prince of Meshech and Tubal in Ezekiel's prophecy (Ezekiel 38).
links.card_of: Tubal: A son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, whose descendants became a distant northern people.

sentences: Ezekiel names Meshech and Tubal among the nations brought down to the pit (Ezekiel 32).
Gog is called chief prince of Meshech and Tubal in Ezekiel's prophecy (Ezekiel 38).
links.card_of: Meshech: A son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, whose descendants became a distant northern people.

sentences: A distant northern people and land, often named with Tubal.
Ezekiel prophesied against Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (Ezekiel 38).
links.card_of: Meshech: A distant northern people and land, often named with Tubal.

sentences: God will send survivors to distant nations, including Tubal, to declare his glory (Isaiah 66).
Tubal traded slaves and bronze vessels with the merchants of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Gog is called chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and God declares himself against him (Ezekiel 38).
links.card_of: Tubal: A distant nation descended from Japheth, often paired with Meshech, known for trading slaves and bronze.

sentences: Ezekiel prophesies against Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (Ezekiel 38).
links.card_of: Magog: A distant northern land, home of Gog, who leads the nations against God's people.

options.name: Valley of Hinnom
options.who: A valley along the south and west sides of Jerusalem, later notorious for idolatrous child sacrifice.

options.name: Valley of the Son of Hinnom
options.who: A valley south of Jerusalem where idolatrous child sacrifice was practiced.

sentences: Child sacrifice in the Valley of Hinnom will make it the Valley of Slaughter.
Jeremiah smashes a clay flask in the Valley of Hinnom to show that God will shatter Jerusalem.
Judah built high places in the Valley of Hinnom to offer children to Molech (Jeremiah 32).
links.card_of: Molech: A god of the Ammonites associated with child sacrifice, whose worship the LORD forbade.

sentences: A site in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned as offerings.
links.card_of: Topheth: A site in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned as offerings.

sentences: Judah's boundary ran up the Valley of Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city (Joshua 15).
Benjamin's border went down the Valley of Hinnom, south of the Jebusite slope (Joshua 18).
links.card_of: Jebusite: The ridge of the Jebusite city, Jerusalem, used as a landmark on Judah's northern boundary.

sentences: Jeremiah's name of judgment for the Valley of Hinnom, where children were sacrificed.
links.card_of: Valley of Slaughter: Jeremiah's name of judgment for the Valley of Hinnom, where children were sacrificed.

options.name: Zephaniah
options.who: A priest, son of Maaseiah, in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.

options.name: Zephaniah
options.who: A prophet in the days of King Josiah who warned of the day of the LORD.

sentences: Zephaniah warns Judah and the nations of the coming day of the LORD and promises joy for a humble remnant.
Zephaniah prophesies during the reign of Josiah king of Judah.
Zephaniah announces that the day of the LORD will sweep away Judah's idolaters and complacent people.
Zephaniah urges the humble to seek the LORD and announces judgment on Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush, and Assyria.
Father of Zephaniah, a leading priest in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.
His son Zephaniah was sent by Zedekiah to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD (Jeremiah 21).
Shemaiah wrote from Babylon urging his son Zephaniah to restrain Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29).
links.card_of: Maaseiah: Father of Zephaniah, a leading priest in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.

sentences: He wrote to the priest Zephaniah, urging him to put Jeremiah in the stocks (Jeremiah 29).
Zephaniah read the letter to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29).
links.card_of: Shemaiah: Shemaiah of Nehelam, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon who opposed Jeremiah.

sentences: Zephaniah announced judgment on those who swear by the Lord and yet by Milcom (Zephaniah 1).
links.card_of: Milcom: The detestable god of the Ammonites, whose worship Solomon brought into Israel and Josiah later abolished.

sentences: The father of the prophet Zephaniah and a descendant of Hezekiah through Gedaliah and Amariah.
The word of the LORD came to Zephaniah son of Cushi in the days of King Josiah (Zephaniah 1).
links.card_of: Cushi: The father of the prophet Zephaniah and a descendant of Hezekiah through Gedaliah and Amariah.

sentences: Zephaniah foresaw worshipers bringing offerings from beyond the rivers of Cush (Zephaniah 3).
links.card_of: Cush: The land south of Egypt along the upper Nile.

sentences: Zephaniah warns that a cry will rise from the Fish Gate on the day of the LORD (Zephaniah 1).
links.card_of: Fish Gate: A gate in Jerusalem's northern wall, probably named for the fish market nearby.

sentences: Zephaniah foretold a wail from the Second Quarter on the day of the LORD (Zephaniah 1).
links.card_of: Second Quarter: A newer district of Jerusalem where the prophetess Huldah lived in Josiah's day.

sentences: Shemaiah had written to the priest Zephaniah, urging him to confine Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29).
links.card_of: Nehelam: The home or family of Shemaiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.

options.name: Zichri
options.who: A Levite of the Kohathite clan, son of Izhar and brother of Korah.

options.name: Zichri
options.who: A Benjaminite whose son Joel was overseer of the Benjaminites living in Jerusalem after the exile.

sentences: He is listed as a son of Kohath, with sons Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri (Exodus 6).
links.card_of: Izhar: Levite son of Kohath and father of Korah, ancestor of the Izharite clan.

sentences: He served with Joel son of Zichri, the overseer of the Benjaminites there (Nehemiah 11).
links.card_of: Judah: A Benjaminite son of Hassenuah who was second in charge over Jerusalem after the exile.

options.name: Ziph
options.who: A town in the hill country of Judah, southeast of Hebron, beside a wilderness.

options.name: Ziph
options.who: A town in the Negev of Judah toward Edom, distinct from Ziph near Hebron.

options.name: Ziph
options.who: A man of Judah listed as a son of Jehallelel in the tribe's genealogy.

sentences: Tiria is listed among the sons of Jehallelel, with Ziph, Ziphah, and Asarel (1 Chronicles 4).
links.card_of: Tiria: A man of Judah, son of Jehallelel, named in the tribe's genealogy.

sentences: Ziphah is named among the sons of Jehallelel, with Ziph, Tiria, and Asarel (1 Chronicles 4).
links.card_of: Ziphah: A man of Judah, son of Jehallelel, listed in the tribe's genealogy.

sentences: Ziph was allotted to Judah in the hill country (Joshua 15).
David took Saul's spear and water jar in the wilderness of Ziph (1 Samuel 26).
links.card_of: Ziph: A town in the hill country of Judah, southeast of Hebron, beside a wilderness.

sentences: A place in the wilderness of Ziph where David hid from Saul.
David hides at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph while Saul seeks his life (1 Samuel 23).
links.card_of: Horesh: A place in the wilderness of Ziph where David hid from Saul.

sentences: A hill in the wilderness near Ziph where David hid from Saul.
links.card_of: Hachilah: A hill in the wilderness near Ziph where David hid from Saul.

sentences: A town in the Negev of Judah toward Edom, distinct from Ziph near Hebron.
Ziph is listed among Judah's southernmost towns toward the border of Edom (Joshua 15).
A different Ziph appears later in the same list among the hill-country towns (Joshua 15).
links.card_of: Ziph: A town in the Negev of Judah toward Edom, distinct from Ziph near Hebron.

sentences: It belonged to a group of ten towns with their villages, including Maon, Carmel, and Ziph (Joshua 15).
links.card_of: Kain: A town in the hill country of Judah, listed near Zanoah, Gibeah, and Timnah.
